description: Faceted violet, plum deepening to lilac, with a thumbnail of gold at the middle that looks written rather than grown.
lore: Every facet on one is a one-off; the mark is not. Two strokes and a splayed foot, in gold, small enough to hide under a thumbnail, identical down to the stroke on every stone ever brought in. Off a creature that is [[monsters/butterfly_dragon|nothing but retellings]], the piece that pressed hardest was the one thing all its tellers' countries remember alike: gold, which does not drift. Set in a blade it lends tempo — the stroke arrives as if it had been made once already.

The mark is also why it is the most forged stone on any bench. Violet glass lumps well, and a forger with real gold gets the mark right every time, gold being the point of gold. [[characters/54bead23|Osric]], new enough to still count in living years, bought one cheap off a stranger at his first market and carried it to [[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] for setting. She drew it once through her hearth ash and handed it back grey. Ash will not sit on a true one — one wipe and it is finished — and the glass kept its coat. It hangs over his forge door now with the price scratched underneath, and he takes the ribbing better than he would take the sympathy.
